content.executive_summary:
- **Frontier Coding Leader (Vendor-Reported)**: Claude Opus 4.8 hits 69.2% on SWE-bench Pro vs. GLM 5.1 at 58.4% and GPT-5.4 at 57.7%; on the standardized Scale SEAL run, GPT-5.4 (xHigh) takes the lead at 59.1% with Muse Spark at 55.0% and Opus 4.6 (thinking) at 51.9% -> Hermes should default the "frontier tier" to **Opus 4.8 (effort=high)** for hard-architecture tasks and route UP only when Opus itself fails twice.
- **Cost-Per-Solved-Point Champion**: Claude Haiku 4.5 sits at ~$0.13 of output per SWE-bench Pro point, vs. ~$0.25 for GPT-5.4 and ~$0.26 for Gemini 3.1 Pro -> Route the bulk of subagent/tool-execution traffic through **Haiku 4.5** and save 60-70% on daily volume.
- **Open-Weights Frontrunner**: GLM 5.2 (released June 16, 2026) scores 62.1 on SWE-bench Pro and 81.0 on Terminal-Bench 2.1, trailing Opus 4.8 by ~1 point on FrontierSWE and ~13 points on SWE-Marathon -> Use **GLM 5.2 on Fireworks** ($1.40/$4.40 per M, 80% cache hit discount at $0.26/M) as an MIT-licensed escape hatch when quota or cost caps bite.
- **Long-Horizon Workhorse**: Claude Sonnet 4.6 carries the 1M context window (beta) with "context compaction," adaptive thinking, programmatic tool calling, and 80.2% on SWE-bench Verified -> Route full-repo retrieval, large migrations, and "memory-heavy" agent sessions through **Sonnet 4.6** rather than Opus.
- **Latency-Tier Winner**: Claude Haiku 4.5 runs 4-5x faster than Sonnet 4.5 at one-third the cost; GPT-5.4 mini (xhigh) reaches 60.0% Terminal-Bench 2.0 with strong perf/latency tradeoff -> Token-efficient and live-coding subtasks should ride **Haiku 4.5** or **GPT-5.4 mini**.
- **Real-World Routing Evidence**: Tyler Folkman's 2,415-turn audit landed at $76.77 (94% cheaper than all-GPT-5.5), with 82.2% of turns handled by Kimi K2.6 at $64.79, GPT-5.5 reserved for 9.9% of "earned" turns, and GLM 5.1 used at <1% -> The cheapest-fallback-by-default pattern measurably matches frontier quality in production.
- **Tool-Use Reliability Gap**: GPT-5.4 mini scores 42.9% on Toolathon but 93.4% on φ42-bench (telecom); Opus 4.8 leads computer use at 84% on Online-Mind2Web -> Tool-error tolerance is parameter-dependent, so Hermes should record per-tool failure counts and re-route after two consecutive tool errors.
- **Cache Economics Floor**: Anthropic prompt cache break-even is roughly 3 reads per write within the 5-minute TTL; cache writes cost 1.25x of base and reads 0.1x -> Hermes must structure prompts so tool definitions and system prompts become stable cache prefixes and only the diff pushes to the model.
- **Open-Weight 90% Routing Pattern**: Magnitude reports "60% less than Claude Code with no drop in performance" by running 90% on open models and escalating only on hard traces -> A pure cost-driven production strategy is genuinely viable; the 10% frontier tail preserves quality where it matters.
- **Provider Agility Is Built-In**: Hermes Agent from Nous Research uses OPENAI_BASE_URL to swap between vLLM, OpenRouter, NVIDIA NIM, and the Nous Portal without code changes -> Hermes-stack design should treat the router as the abstraction and providers as replaceable implementations.
- **Risk Failure Case**: One Reddit tester said "Opus 4.6 is fast but lacks depth, whereas GPT 5.4 goes deeper but is a bit slower" when given the same task in Claude Code vs. Codex -> The same harness can produce different outcomes on the same prompt, so routing by model alone is not enough; Hermes must also pin the harness (claude-code, codex-cli, opencode) per route.
- **Verification Gap**: "Vendor-reported" SWE-bench Pro scores run 10-30 points above standardized Scale SEAL scores; some "Claude Fable" entries on the morphllm leaderboard appear inflated or synthetic -> Prefer standardized + Scale SEAL numbers for routing thresholds; treat vendor scores as ceiling estimates.

### Claude Opus 4.8 (Frontier Tier, May 28, 2026)

Opus 4.8 is Anthropic's most capable engine. Pricing is $5/M input and $25/M output in regular mode and $10/$50 in "fast" mode (2.5x speed). The model exposes five effort levels (low / medium / high / extra / max) via the budget_tokens/effort parameter; **high** is the default and **max** produces noticeable quality only on genuinely complex tasks where errors are costly. On computer use, Opus 4.8 leads with 84% on Online-Mind2Web. Failure mode in practice: Reddit's vibecoding thread notes that "Opus 4.8 is definitely more stable than 4.7 [but] tends to hallucinate shader optimizations and can lose context on lower-level GPU memory." ### Case Study 1: Tyler Folkman's 2,415-Turn Audit

Folkman published a Substack audit where 2,415 agent turns across 6 models cost **$76.77** - a 94% saving vs. all-GPT-5.5. The router uses 8 model paths; real usage split was Kimi K2.6 at 82.2% (1,984 turns, $64.79), GPT-5.5 at 9.9% (238 turns, $11.04) for "max" reasoning on hard architecture or repeated failures, and local Qwen 3.6 27B at 4.4% (106 turns, $0.00) for private prompts. GLM 5.1 was used at 0.9% of turns (21 turns, $0.15). Folkman concludes that "most turns did not need frontier intelligence" and that DeepSeek V4 Flash "delivers 82% of Claude Opus 4.7's SWE-Bench Pro score at roughly 1/36th of the input price." His selection signal was a value_score = SWE-Bench Pro score / input dollars per M tokens. [real_world_routing_patterns_and_case_studies[0]] [75]

Magnitude is a coding agent that "runs entirely on open models" and "costs 60% less than Claude Code with no drop in performance." Architecture is a "strong leader" model that escalates only "when the work demands it." Pass-through API pricing with no markup and $5 free credits. Backed by Y Combinator. Implication: a pure cost-driven open-weights strategy is now production-viable - the 10% frontier tail preserves quality where it matters. [real_world_routing_patterns_and_case_studies[1]] [76]

content.synthesis_a_concrete_routing_policy_for_:
The strongest pattern across Folkman's audit, Magnitude's design, the Mindstudio effort table, and the Magnitude 90/10 model is a **four-tier cascade with explicit escalations**. Tier 0 (parsing, classification, simple extraction) is reserved for the cheapest model that still passes task type. Tier 1 (subagent tool execution and live interactive coding) is the sweet spot for fractional cost. Tier 2 is the workhorse that handles retrieval, planning, and review. Tier 3 (frontier with full thinking budget) is reserved for repo-migration, diff synthesis, and any task where Tier 2 has failed twice.

### Recommended Stack (June 2026)

| Layer | Model | Provider | Role | Trigger |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Tier 0 - Subagent Noise | GPT-5.4 nano | OpenAI or Azure | classification, log triage, regex-style extraction | input length < 4K, no tool calls |
| Tier 0 - Subagent Noise | Claude Haiku 4.5 | Anthropic | classification, log triage | consulting Anthropic stack |
| Tier 0 - Subagent Noise | Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite | Google AI Studio | classification < 8K | cost-critical batch |
| Tier 1 - Tool Execution & Live Coding | Claude Haiku 4.5 | Anthropic | subagent orchestration, tool loops, real-time user feedback | "more than twice the speed" of Sonnet and 90% of its capability |
| Tier 1 - Tool Execution & Live Coding | GPT-5.4 mini xhigh | OpenAI | Toolathon-tuned mini, "subagents in parallel" | Toolathon weight ≥0.4 use case |
| Tier 1 - Tool Execution & Live Coding | Gemini 2.5 Flash | Google AI Studio | when 1M context is useful and budget tight | context > 200K, sub-dollar-per-M routes |
| Tier 2 - Workhorse | Claude Sonnet 4.6 (effort=high) | Anthropic | planning, large retrieval, full-repo summarization, code review, "memory-heavy" sessions | default for new tasks |
| Tier 2 - Workhorse | GPT-5.4 (effort=high) | OpenAI | architecture work where "GPT 5.4 goes deeper" per Reddit | harness=codex-cli or opencode |
| Tier 2 - Workhorse | GLM 5.2 | Fireworks or OpenRouter | MIT-licensed open weights for cost ceiling, batch | budget or quota bound on Tier 2 |
| Tier 3 - Frontier | Claude Opus 4.8 (effort=high, then max) | Anthropic | Errors in Tier 2 twice, repo-scale migration, dynamic workflows | Tier 2 fail-2 escalation |
| Tier 3 - Frontier | GPT-5.4 Pro or xhigh | OpenAI | Terminal-Bench 2.0 75.1% leader, GDPval 83% | where Anthropic is throttled |
| Tier 3 - Frontier | Gemini 3.1 Pro (thinking high) | Google AI Studio | SWE-bench Verified 80.6%, batch path | 50% batch discount and non-urgent jobs |

### Routing Policy (decision logic)

1. **Default task entry**: Tier 2 (Sonnet 4.6 effort=high). If task is fully classified (single-tool, no reasoning) and prompt < 4K, drop to Tier 1 (Haiku 4.5) or Tier 0 (nano/Flash-Lite).
2. **Subagent fan-out**: Any sub-task launched by the main agent uses Tier 1 by default and is pinned to Haiku 4.5 if running on Anthropic, GPT-5.4 mini if on OpenAI, or Gemini 2.5 Flash if context > 200K.
3. **Tool-error escalation**: If a subagent fails two consecutive tool calls on the same tool, escalate that subagent to Tier 2 and the tool's reliability counter rolls a metric the harness uses to gate Tier 3 access.
4. **Cost ceiling**: When the daily Anthropic bill exceeds a configured price, redirect Tier 2 traffic to GLM 5.2 (Fireworks or OpenRouter) by setting `OPENAI_BASE_URL` to the GLM endpoint - Hermes' provider-agnostic integration means this is a one-line change.
5. **Long horizon**: When the conversation context exceeds 400K tokens, route to Sonnet 4.6 with context compaction enabled, or to Gemini 3.1 Pro (thinking) with the 1M boundary in mind (and recall 26.3% MRCR at 1M).
6. **Caching**: Use Anthropic prompt cache (5-min TTL, 1.25x write, ~0.1x read) by separating tool definitions + system prompt as the stable prefix. Break-even is ~3 reads per write per hour, so Hermes should batch turns inside that window whenever possible.
7. **Batch and discount paths**: For repo-scale migrations and offline sweeps, prefer the Gemini 50% batch path or the Fireworks cache-hit rate ($0.26/M on GLM 5.2).
8. **Effort dispatch**: When sending to Opus 4.8, start at effort=high and ramp to max only after evidence the task is genuinely complex; the Mindstudio data shows the quality difference between high and max is "negligible" on simple tasks but real on math/architecture.

### Failure Modes to Watch

- **Same prompt, different harness**: A Reddit coder reports "Opus 4.6 is fast but lacks depth, whereas GPT 5.4 goes deeper" comparing Claude Code vs. Codex on identical prompts. Hermes must pin the harness per route, not just the model.
- **In-flight inflation**: Vendor scores run 10-30 points above Scale SEAL standardized scores, and recent "Claude Fable 5" and "Claude Fable Latest" entries on morphllm appear inflated. Pin routing thresholds to standardized scores.
- **Gemini 3.1 Pro variance**: Top SWE-bench score but Reddit users report "nowhere near as reliable or capable as Claude Opus 4.6 or GPT 5.4 for real-world coding." Treat the 80.6% as ceiling.
- **Cache write penalty**: Writes cost 1.25x of base and reads 0.1x. If a turn only reads once, caching is net negative.
- **GLM tool anti-hack**: GLM 5.2's "anti-hack module" actively blocks raw curl operations. If Hermes relies on `curl` for proxying, expect refusals - plan around `requests` or `httpx` inside the harness.

### Providers and Cost Tools

- **Anthropic**: Direct API; Claude Code SDK; Anthropic prompt cache for Sonnet/Opus.
- **OpenAI**: Direct API; Codex CLI; ChatGPT Enterprise gateway.
- **Google**: AI Studio for 2.5 Pro/Flash; Vertex AI for enterprise; batch API at 50% off.
- **OpenRouter**: GLM 5.2, Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini in one bill; auto-router for fallbacks.
- **Fireworks**: GLM 5.2 day-zero with $0.26 cache-hit tokens; vLLM-compatible.
- **Together AI, Novita, DeepInfra**: GLM 5.2 mirrors; useful for region-specific serving.
- **vLLM**: Hermes-Nous-style self-hosting when privacy or cost ceiling applies.
- **OpenShift AI**: Production Hermes deployment per Red Hat guide; works with NVIDIA NIM.
